debate_title: Do AI benchmark scores predict real-world usefulness?

conflicts.point: Whether mandatory pre-deployment safety gates enforced through federal procurement rules are required alongside runtime monitoring.

positions.stance: Pre-deployment safety gates and static weight reviews create prohibitive compliance bottlenecks and cannot keep pace with iterative updates, making runtime edge monitoring the superior governance model.

Runtime anomaly detection functions as a symptom-checker that cannot diagnose structural defects embedded in proprietary weights, requiring mandatory pre-deployment gates to prevent irreversible failures.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory pre-deployment safety gates enforced through federal procurement rules are required alongside runtime monitoring.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position draws on established precedent from commercial aviation where runtime error-checking cannot discover foundational structural flaws. The accelerationist claim relies on assertions about speed without demonstrating that runtime tools can diagnose proprietary weight defects.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that runtime anomaly detection successfully identifies and stops hidden structural weight defects in deployed models without pre-market blueprint inspections.
